subject: Is there a way to get predicted classes instead of probabilities per class for the categorical model

messages.author: a0f5c47e0d2e4773
messages.subject: Is there a way to get predicted classes instead of probabilities per class for the categorical model
parts:
For a binary logistic model I get the predicted classes simply by rounding, ie:

predicted_data <- as.data.frame(predict(logit.brm, scale="response"))
round(predicted_data$Estimate)

I can even feed it to the confusionMatrix from the caret package like so confusionMatrix(round(predicted_data$Estimate), predicted_data$Estimate)

For multinomial / categorical models in brms this doesn't work, since for 3+ response levels the probability of any individual response may not be above .5.

What I'd really like is something comparable to nnet's predict for its multinom function. For this, all I have to do is type predict(multinom.fit, dataframe). For instance, let's say I am using the iris dataset. After fitting the model, predict(iris.fit , iris) returns a vector of the classifications:

[1] setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa
[21] setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa
[51] virginica virginica virginica versicolor virginica versicolor virginica versicolor virginica versicolor
[61] versicolor versicolor versicolor versicolor versicolor virginica versicolor versicolor versicolor

Is there a way to get brms to do this? I've been searching around the net and playing around with the predict and fitted functions but I can't seem to get this kind of output.

parts:
That seems to just return the highest probability, rather than a character vector with "virginica", etc or 1,2,3. 

For the example I have the iris data set in R fit to a model : multi.brm = brm(Species ~ Septal.Length, data=iris, family=categorical) for instance.

 Then I run

predicted_data = predict(multi.brm, iris). 
apply(predicted_data, 1, max)

and get a vector of the highest probability for each of three outcomes rather than something like what the multinom predict function gives. I'm not sure if what I am asking is possible unless it were specifically programmed in brms that way.

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Is there a way to get predicted classes instead of probabilities per class for the categorical model
parts:
Sorry, it whould be argmax not max. Since R has no built in function for argmax, we just define it ourselves:

predicted_data = predict(multi.brm, iris)
argmax <- function(x) match(max(x), x)
apply(predicted_data, 1, argmax)
